Numerous large trees were blown down near Lanesboro with some of these uprooted. Some of the trees fell on tents but no injuries occurred as the campers had taken shelter.
A wind gust of 67 mph occurred near Kasson.
The automated weather observing equipment at the Preston airport measured a wind gust of 62 mph.
Trees were blown down onto power lines in Ostrander.
Several trees were blown down in Austin. Some homes and vehicles were damaged by the fallen trees. Around 700 customers lost power because of the storm damage.
Several large trees were blown down.

An EF-1 tornado passed through rural Buffalo County north of Cream. The tornado was on the ground for about three-quarters of a mile and damaged a house and some outbuildings, including a large machine shed.

An EF-1 tornado passed through rural Buffalo County north of Waumandee. The tornado was on the ground for about a half mile and removed the second floor of a hunting structure. Significant crop damage also occurred.
In Alma, significant tree damage occurred, windows were broken and damage occurred to the cemetery.
A large tree limb was blown down southwest of Austin. The limb landed on a vehicle damaging the hood.
Several large tree branches were blown down in Osage.
Numerous large tree branches were blown down in New Hampton.
A large tree branch was blown down in Decorah.
A grain bin was destroyed, the roof was blown off a machine shed and trees were uprooted on a farm southwest of Mitchell.

The roof was blown off a building in Mabel.
A steel framed outbuilding was destroyed northeast of Mantorville. The debris was blown into and damaged a grain bin.
The roof was blown off a building near Lanesboro.
Trees were snapped off and uprooted in Soldiers Grove. Some of these trees landed on houses and vehicles.
Trees were blown down on the southwest side of Austin.
Trees were blown down in Medford.
Trees were blown down across various parts of Taylor County.
Numerous trees were blown down in Thorp. The fire chief estimated the wind gust speed to be around 60 mph.
Numerous trees were blown down in and near Big Flats.
Power lines and trees were blown down northwest of Necedah.
Trees were blown down in New Lisbon.
Trees were blown down east of Adams that blocked County Road M near the intersection with 10th Avenue.
Several trees were blown down west of Buckhorn State Park.
Some trees were blown down near Brooks.
A large tree branch was blown down and blocked traffic in Hayfield.
Locally heavy rains caused most creeks in and near Bloomington to go out of their banks.
Locally heavy rains in Mt. Hope caused basements to become flooded.
In Mt. Hope, 4.4 inches of rain of fell.
In Harmony, 3.26 inches of rain fell.
Heavy rains caused Deer Creek to go out of its banks and send water over State Highay 139 south of Harmony.
Locally heavy rains pushed the Upper Iowa River out of its banks sending water over County Road W14 east of Kendallville.
Locally heavy rain caused numerous washouts on Roanoke Avenue between 200th and 270th Streets in eastern Chickasaw County.
The COOP observer in Eyota measured 3.88 inches of rain.
The COOP observer in Monona measured 4.87 inches of rain.
Locally heavy rains produced flash flooding in the Whitewater State Park. This flooding washed out some trail bridges and flooded campsites.
Locally heavy rains pushed the Fennimore Fork out of its banks sending water over Witek Road northeast of Fennimore.
Locally heavy rains pushed the Martin Branch of the Little Grant River out of its banks sending water over Govier and Marian Roads northwest of Lancaster.
Locally heavy rains caused water flowing through a drainage ditch to go over Ready Hollow Road near County Highway X north of Bagley. The high water caused the road to be temporarily closed.
Trees and branches were blown down in Lansing. Boat docks were damaged when the wind pushed some boats several feet upstream and onto the shore.
Trees were blown down northeast of Loyal.
The aircraft control operators at the Rochester airport observed a funnel cloud.
A funnel cloud was sighted southwest of Kasson.
A funnel cloud was sighted north of Le Roy.
A funnel cloud was sighted near the Iowa state line southwest of Adams.
A funnel cloud was sighted near Rock Creek.
Numerous trees were blown down in Stewartville. The debris from a destroyed metal grain bin became wrapped around a snapped off power pole.
An EF-0 tornado touched down in rural Vernon County near Retreat. The tornado was on the ground for about three-quarters of a mile and damaged trees and crops along its path.
Trees were blown down near West Concord.
North of Mabel, trees were blown down in a church cemetery damaging some headstones. Windows in the church were broken from a downed branch.
Large tree branches were blown down in Lewiston.
Around two dozen trees were blown down in the township of Maxville.
Locally heavy rains in Austin caused street flooding to occur and washed out a portion of an enbankment along Turtle Creek. 2.97 inches of rain fell on the southwest side of Austin.
A fire was started in a house on the northwest side of Rochester from a lightning strike. The fire caused damaged to the roof and trusses of the house.
Heat indices topped out between 105 and 115 on both the 21st and 22nd. The highest reported het index was 120 from a mesonet reporting station in the Yellow River State Park.
Heat indices topped out between 105 and 115 on both the 21st and 22nd. The highest reported heat index was 109 from a mesonet reporting station near Ionia.

Locally heavy rain pushed a branch of the Sny Magill Creek out of its banks. The flooding caused the Paradise Valley Campground to be evacuated. The campground was extensively damaged, with picnic tables destroyed, gazebos washed away, a small building moved several feet, roads damaged and there was two feet of standing water in the office building.
Locally heavy rain pushed the North Cedar Creek out of its banks causing damage to Ivory Road.
Runoff from heavy rain caused the Whitewater River to go out its banks in the Whitewater River State Park. The river crested less than a half foot above flood stage at 13.65 feet.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Platte River out of its banks near Rockville. The river crested less than a foot over the flood stage at 9.8 feet.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Grant River out of its banks near Burton. The river crested almost three above the flood stage at 20.82 feet.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Turkey River out of its banks in Spillville. The river crested less than a half foot above the flood stage at 9.21 feet.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Turkey River out of its banks near Eldorado. The river crested around a foot and a half above the flood stage at 14.55 feet.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Turkey River out of its banks in Elkader. The river crested less than a half foot above the flood stage at 12.21 feet.
A wind gust of 60 mph occurred at the NWS La Crosse office blowing down several branches.
An estimated 60 mph wind gust occurred on the south side of Holmen. Numerous trees were snapped off or uprooted.
An estimated 60 mph wind gust occurred on the north side of La Crosse. Several small trees were blown down and minor street flooding also occurred.

Numerous trees were blown down in West Salem along with power lines. A tree was split in half with the section that came down blocking a part of the street. Nearly 1,500 residences were without power after the storm.
Several large trees were blown down along County Highway M south of West Salem.

Locally heavy rain caused street flooding to occur in the city of La Crosse. Liberty Street  near Madison was briefly impassable because of the flooding. At least two vehicles became stuck in the street flooding.
Damage to corn fields occurred in the Cashton area from thunderstorm wind gusts.

Hundreds of trees were damaged or uprooted in Holmen. Especially hard hit was the Remington Hills subdivision where at least one tree fell on a house. After the storm, over 500 residents were without power.
Several trees were blown down in Decorah.
The automated weather observing equipment at the Decorah airport measured a wind gust of 63 mph.
Several large trees and some power lines were blown down near Union Center. A pickup truck was damaged when a tree fell on it.
Power lines were blown down in Potosi.
A Postal Service employee reported driving through a lot of hail, some of which was up to the size of pennies.
Several large trees were blow down near Kendallville. Some farm buildings and a grain bin were also damaged.
Tree limbs were blown down just west of Hazel Green.
An estimated 60 mph wind gust occurred in the city of La Crosse.
A wind gust of 71 mph was measured on the south side of Holmen.
Large trees were blown down south of Clayton.

Runoff from heavy rain caused several streams to go out of their banks sending water over State Highway 93 near Eleva, State Highway 121 west of Elk Creek and County Highways D, E, O, Y and OO east of Elk Creek and south of Strum. The flood waters from Elk Creek stranded residences in the village of Elk Creek. A section of road was washed out at the intersection of State Highway 93 and County Highway H south of Eleva. Numerous culverts were washed out which caused State Highway 93 to be closed near Eleva. State Highway 93 was also impassable north of Elk Creek where flooding from a branch of the Chimney Rock Creek covered the road. The Buffalo River Recreation trail was washed out in several locations and closed as well.

Runoff from heavy rain pushed numerous streams out of their banks across Buffalo County. In addition, mudslides occurred and some bridges were washed out. Five families in Mondovi and Gilmanton were displaced from their homes because of the flooding. In Gilmanton, flood waters from Elk Creek surrounded some houses and water rescues had to be performed to get the residents safely out. Just west of Gilmanton along County Highway B, several feet of flood waters from Elk Creek flowed through 5 homes. State Highways 37 and 88 near Gilmanton were closed because of the flood waters. State Highway 35 south of Alma also had water over the road for a while in the morning. The flash flooding caused a deep hole to form in County Highway N near State Highway 37 northeast of Alma. A 15 foot section of road was washed out near State Highway 88 and County Highway U south of Gilmanton. Household LP tanks were moved by the flood waters and were seen floating down the Little Waumandee Creek near Cream. State Highway 88 and County Highway E near Cream were closed when water from the Little Waumandee Creek covered the roads. State Highway 121 was closed east of Gilmanton when flood waters from a branch of the South Fork Elk Creek covered the road. 1 to 2 feet of water was over State Highway 88 northeast of Cochrane near the intersection with County Highway O. Fifteen homeowners applied for federal assistance after suffering damage to more than half of their homes.
Near Nelson, 6.3 inches of rain fell.
Several washouts and mudslides occurred on U.S. Highway 61 south of Lake City and along County Roads 4 and 10.
Water covered County Highway Q northwest of Independence.
Runoff from heavy rains caused landslides to occur that undermined several roads in the vicinity of Urne.
In Urne, 5.5 inches of rain fell.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed most of the streams in the vicinity of Stetsonville out of their banks, including Creel Creek.
In Buffalo City, 5 inches of rain fell.
Near Dorchester, 3.32 inches of rain fell.
In Medford, 4.33 inches of rain fell.
In Kellogg, 7.67 inches of rain fell.
Near Alma, 5.06 inches of rain fell.
Near Reads Landing, 6.3 inches of rain fell.
In the city of Wabasha, 6.6 inches of rain fell.

Near Theilman, County Road 86 had a washout and debris over the road and a mudslide covered a portion of County Road 4. Flood waters from West Indian Creek rushed through a campground, damaging several campers and took out a snowmobile bridge.
Water covered a section of County Road 42 southwest of Kellogg.

Flood waters moving downstream through Elk Creek caused Bugle Lake in Independence to flood. As the water levels rose, evacuations of businesses and residences near the lake occurred. The flood waters covered Elm Street and went into the basements of several houses.
A funnel cloud was sighted near Dodge Center.
Several reports of funnel clouds were received from the Kasson area.
A funnel cloud was sighted near Claremont.
More funnel clouds were sighted in Kasson.
A funnel cloud was sighted near West Concord.
A funnel cloud was sighted near West Union.
Large tree branches were blown down in Mapleview.
An estimated 60 mph wind gust occurred in Hayfield. The wind gust moved a gazebo and blew down a large tree.
A large tree was uprooted in Austin.
Estimated wind gusts of 60 to 65 mph occurred in Rock Dell.
An estimated 60 mph wind gust occurred in Stewartville.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Cherry Grove.
Lots of trees were blown down northwest of Spring Valley.
Trees were blown down in the extreme southwest part of Dodge County west of Hayfield.
A 73 mph wind gust occurred at the Preston airport.
Numerous trees were blown down or damaged west of Preston.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down along State Highway 35 from De Soto south toward the Rush Creek area.
A road was blocked in Boscobel when a large tree was blown down.
Small trees were blown down in Bagley.
A large tree was blown down in Nelson Dewey State Park.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed Elk Creek out of its banks causing water to go over State Highway 93 near County Highway E. State Highway 93 was closed between Eleva and Independence.
Heavy rains caused standing water to cover County Highway E northwest of Tunnel City.
Heavy rains caused street flooding to occur in parts of the city of La Crosse.
Runoff from heavy rains caused flooding to occur in Mondovi.
Runoff from heavy rains caused Farrington Creek to go out of its banks with water covering County Road A west of Mondovi.
County Highway B was closed between Sand Road and State Highway 88 northwest of Gilmanton when flood waters from Elk Creek went over the road.
Flood waters from Elk Creek seeped into some of the same houses that were affected by flooding in the August 11th event.
An estimated 65 mph wind gust occurred in Rushford that blew down trees and power lines. Some pea sized hail also occurred.
A 32' x 172' dairy barn was blown down near Racine and another outbuilding was damaged.

Runoff from heavy rains caused flooding to occur in and around Calmar, Fort Atkinson and Spillville. The flood waters caused the basement of one house to collapse in Calmar. Cars became stranded near U.S. Highway 52 around Calmar with one person having to stand on top of a car to get out of the flood waters. Rogers Creek near Fort Atkinson went out of its banks with water over several secondary roads. Flooding also occurred along Bohemian Creek in the western part of the county. Flood waters were knee deep in some residences and caused evacuations to occur near Ludwig County Park and County Highway B16 was closed due to the flood waters northwest of Spillville. Sandbagging efforts in Spillville had to be stopped because the water was rising too fast on Bohemian Creek and the Turkey River. The flood waters from the Turkey River isolated Spillville and prevented anyone from leaving or entering the town. One bridge near Spillville sustained damage from a tree swept up in the flood waters. Early estimates by the mayor of Spillville indicated 9 homes were seriously affected with water on the first floor and another 20 to 25 sustained less damage with water mainly in the basements.

Flood waters caused homes along Cedar Valley Road, southwest of Freeport, to be evacuated. Widespread flooding occurred in Freeport prompting the need for water rescues to be performed and for local law enforcement to not allow any travel in the area. River Road near Freeport was closed due to flooding from the Upper Iowa River that also caused a trailer court to be evacuated. The runoff from heavy rains also caused urban flooding to occur on the south side of Decorah where a vehicle was flooded in a parking lot. Numerous bridge approaches were lost in the flooding and lots of gravel was washed off roads.
Wind damage occurred at a farm between Ontario and Hillsboro breaking large branches off trees and flipping trailers.
A large machine shed at a farm was blown down.
Several large trees were blown down on the south side of town.
Numerous trees were blown down along Wabasha County Road 7.
Numerous trees were blown down or shredded in about a 100 feet wide swath as intense thunderstorm winds came across Battle Island and into the Blackhawk Park campground.
A roof was damaged and numerous trees were blown down along Iowa River Drive southeast of Dorchester.
Runoff from heavy rain caused flooding to occur along Beaver Creek in the vicinity of Bassett.

Runoff from heavy rain caused flooding to occur along Watsons Creek. The flood waters went over Addison Road north of Riceville. Flooding also occurred along the Little Cedar River in the vicinity of Stacyville. Sandbagging operations were performed northwest of Osage in an effort to protect residences from flooding along Sugar Creek.

Runoff from heavy rain caused flooding to occur in Lansing along Clear Creek. Two people had to be rescued when the cabin they were sleeping in was moved off its foundation. The cabin became lodged against some trees allowing rescuers to reach them with a boat. The cabin was destroyed. 5.2 inches of rain was reported around 130 a.m. The runoff also caused a mudslide to occur north of Lansing.
Runoff from heavy rain caused flooding to occur in and around Waukon. Several rescues had to be performed to save people from the flooding. Some businesses and homes were damaged by the flooding.

One person had to be rescued near Steuben when an attempt to drive through flood waters caused the vehicle to be swept off the road. Runoff from heavy rain caused a mudslide to occur near Bell Center. The mudslide brought down trees and covered County Highway S. Other mudslides occurred west of Steuben and covered State Highway 179.
A mesonet reporting station south of Dorchester measured 5.67 inches of rain.
A mesonet reporting station northeast of Riceville measured 4.26 inches of rain.
A mesonet reporting station in Steuben measured 5.61 inches of rain.
The COOP observer west of Ionia measured 3.68 inches of rain.
Runoff from heavy rain caused flooding in a large share of the county. The flood waters covered numerous roads throughout the county.
The COOP observer in Osage measured 4.73 inches of rain.
Flood waters from the Kickapoo River were about 1.5 feet over County Highway S near Bell Center.

State Highway 9 was closed west of Cresco due to flood waters from the North Branch of the Turkey River. The flood waters from the North Branch of the Turkey River also washed out Robin Avenue. Lidtke County Park just north of Lime Springs was flooded by the Upper Iowa River. A small mudslide occurred along Watsons Creek in Lake Hendricks Park in Riceville. The county engineer estimated there were over 450 locations where water was over roads with only minor damage reported. In Cresco, several houses had water in the basements. School was canceled in the Howard-Winneshiek and Riceville school districts.

Heavy rains caused street flooding to occur in New Hampton with 4 to 5 feet of water reported in some places. Basements in the area were also flooded. Before sunrise on the 24th, water levels continued to rise on many county roads, even those that were not near any rivers or streams. Crane Creek overflowed its banks in Jerico with the flooding primarily limited to agricultural fields and homeowner's yards.
In Riceville, 5.25 inches of rain fell.
A mudslide occurred south of Lynxville that covered both lanes of State Highway 35.
Near Mt. Zion, 5.38 inches of rain fell.
East of Waukon, 7 inches of rain fell.
Flood waters from Trout Creek covered 225th Street southeast of Decorah.
Southeast of New Haven, 7 inches of rain fell.

One person drowned when a vehicle was swept off the road by flood waters from the Little Turkey River. This occurred north of Lawler where Union Avenue crosses the river. The driver called 911 at 340 a.m.
The COOP observer southeast of Decorah measured 7.58 inches of rain.
The COOP observer in Gays Mills measured 5.1 inches of rain.
The COOP observer in New Hampton measured 3.71 inches of rain.
The COOP observer in Elma measured 5.03 inches of rain.
Southeast of Decorah, 8.46 inches of rain was reported.
The automated weather observing equipment at the Decorah airport measured 7.19 inches of rain.
The COOP observer near Cresco measured 6.04 inches of rain.
A house fire in Charles City was started by lightning. Damage to the house was minimal and confined to the attic.
A lightning strike started a house fire west of West Salem. The garage and front half of the house were badly burned while the rest of the structure sustained water and smoke damage.

Runoff from heavy rain caused several streams to go out of their banks across western Richland County. The resulting flood waters caused some roads to be closed including State Highways 56 and 171 along with County Highway F near Excelsior and County Highways E and Q near Boaz.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Trempealeau River out of its banks in Arcadia. The river crested a little more than a foot over the flood stage at 9.18 feet.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Trempealeau River out of its banks in Dodge. The river crested two and a half feet above the flood stage at 11.55 feet.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Trempealeau River briefly out of its banks in Arcadia. The river crested barely above the flood stage at 8.02 feet.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Trempealeau River out of its banks in Dodge. The river crested over a foot above the flood stage at 10.37 feet.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Turkey River out of its banks in Spillville. The river crested over eleven feet above the flood stage at 20.25 feet. This established a new crest of record.

Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Turkey River out of its banks near Eldorado. The river crested at almost nine feet above the flood stage at 21.92 feet. This established a new crest of record. Flooding downstream along the Turkey River damaged some roads and bridges along with county parks.

Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Turkey River out of its banks in Clermont. The river crested over six feet above the flood stage at 22.32 feet. The flood waters damaged the waste water treatment facility.

Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Turkey River out of its banks in Elkader. The river crested over ten feet above the flood stage at 22.57 feet. The flood waters damaged some trails, sidewalks and the riverbank.

Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Turkey River out of its banks in Garber. The river crested over six feet above the flood stage at 23.6 feet. Flooding along the Turkey River throughout the county damaged some roads.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Little Turkey River out of its banks in Waucoma. The flood waters damaged the town's wastewater treatment facility.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Upper Iowa River out of its banks in Bluffton. The river crested less than a half foot above the flood stage at 14.41 feet.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Upper Iowa River out of its banks in Decorah. The river crested around a foot and a half above the flood stage at 13.68 feet.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Upper Iowa River out of its banks near Dorchester. The river crested over ten feet above the flood stage at 24.3 feet. This established a new crest of record.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Cedar River out of its banks near Orchard. The river crested almost two feet above the flood stage at 11.88 feet.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Cedar River out of its banks in Charles City. The river crested just under a foot above the flood stage at 12.96 feet.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Kickapoo River out of its banks in Gays Mills. The river crested less than a foot above the flood stage at 13.73 feet.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Kickapoo River out of its banks in Steuben. The river crested less than a foot above the flood stage at 12.65 feet.
Quarter sized hail fell north of Blair.
Quarter sized hail fell just southwest of Blair.
Quarter sized hail fell at the Black River Falls wastewater treatment facility.
Quarter sized hail fell in Black River Falls.
Trees were blown down in Black River Falls. The locally heavy rain also caused some street flooding to occur.
Large tree branches were blown down north of Mather.
Quarter sized hail fell in Big Flats.
Quarter sized hail fell in Adams.
Winds of 58 mph were reported on the south side of La Crosse.
Flash flooding along Coe Hollow Creek prompted officials to evacuate Sidie Hollow Campground.
Heavy rains caused street flooding to occur in Viroqua.
Flash flooding along the Pine River prompted sandbagging to occur in Yuba. Flooding along Camp Creek caused officials to close State Highway 56 east of Viola.
The COOP observer in Viola measured 4.70 inches of rain.
The observing equipment at the Viroqua airport measured 3.59 inches of rain.
Steam Engine Park in Mabel was flooded by water from Riceford Creek.

A mudslide north of Brownsville caused boulders to tumble down the side of a bluff. One of these boulders hit a house causing considerable damage. Numerous roads in the southern sections of Houston County had water over them prompting officials to close some of them, including State Highway 16 near La Crescent. Flood waters from Winnebago Creek damaged a road in Camp Winnebago south of Caledonia and covered County Highway 5 in the extreme southern part of the county.

Flood waters covered numerous roads across the northern and western sections of Richland County. Roads closed by the flood waters included State Highway 131 north of Viola along the Kickapoo River. State Highway 80 and County Highway C between Yuba and Richland Center were closed because of flooding along the Pine River. Three houses in Yuba had water in the basements. Richland Center schools canceled classes on both the 7th and 8th because of the flooding.
In Purdy, 7.10 inches of rain fell.
The COOP observer in Mabel measured 4.61 inches of rain.
The COOP observer in Caledonia measured 4.41 inches of rain.
The COOP observer near Eitzen measured 5.35 inches of rain.
The COOP observer north of Richland Center measured 3.68 inches of rain.
Flood waters covered some county roads east of Charles City.
Flood waters covered State Highway 24 northeast of Lawler. Many other roads across Chickasaw County were reported to be under water as well.
A boulder came down a bluff side and onto County Highway S near Avalanche.
Flood waters covered Pole Line Road northeast of Frankville.
Debris and rocks from a landslide hit a car at State Highways 35 and 82 south of De Soto.
A landslide pushed a tree onto State Highway 35 south of Ferryville.
Near Floyd, 3.85 inches of rain fell.
In New Hampton, three inches of rain fell.
The COOP observer in Charles City measured 3.35 inches of rain.
Quarter sized hail fell in Bloom City.
Golfball sized hail fell southeast of Garnavillo.
Up to golfball sized hail fell north of Guttenberg.
Quarter sized hail fell southeast of Rockbridge.
Quarter sized hail fell in Glen Haven.
A mudslide sent trees onto one of the southbound lanes of U.S. Highway 61 near Pickwick. The heavy rain also caused water to go over some private driveways along County Highway 19.
A mudslide in De Soto sent debris over one lane of State Highway 82.

Flooding along Beaver Creek created a washout on County Highways T and TT southwest of Ettrick. Another washout occurred east of Ettrick on County Highways D and DD from flooding along the South Branch of Beaver Creek. Some rural township roads were also closed because of flooding. Some street flooding occurred in Arcadia and other small creeks were out of their banks near Ettrick. 2.43 inches of rain was reported in Arcadia and 4.31 inches of rain fell in Ettrick.
At least two mudslides occurred along State Highway 26 between New Albin and Lansing.
Street flooding occurred in Sparta. In addition, water was across several roads over the western portions of the county. Twenty five homes were damaged by the flood waters.

Flood waters from Fleming Creek caused State Highway 108 to be closed near Mindoro.|Water covered low spots in several other locations across the northeast part of La Crosse County. Some of the impacted roads included County Highways C, DE and E. Some minor mudslides also occurred with County Highway OA reduced to one lane. Sixteen homes were damaged by the flooding. Bangor declared a local state of emergency due to flooding along Dutch Creek.
Half dollar sized hail fell in Trempealeau.

Flooding from the South Branch of O'Neill Creek covered County Highway Y south of Chili. Standing water covered State Highway 73 in Christie. The emergency manager reported around 65 locations across the county had water over the road or culverts washed out. Fifteen homes were damaged by the flooding. A state of emergency was declared for the entire county.
A wind gust of 66 mph was measured south of Nora Springs.
A tree was blown down onto a house in Nora Springs.
Trees were blown down west of Rockford.
Trees were blown down in Nora Springs.
Ping pong ball sized hail fell in Rockford.
An estimated wind gust of 70 mph occurred west of Marble Rock.
A weak tornado touched down west of Nashua. The tornado moved through rural areas producing only some crop damage.
Trees, two to three foot in diameter, were blown down just southeast of Marble Rock.
Machine sheds were blown down and destroyed southeast of Marble Rock.

Heavy rain caused water to go over several roads in the southwest two-thirds of Floyd County. The roads were impassable making travel not possible. Water was reported to still be rising southwest of Charles City after sunrise on the 22nd.
A wind gust of 60 mph occurred just west of Marble Rock.
A wind gust of 70 mph occurred just east of Marble Rock.
West of Nashua, 7.55 inches of rain fell.

Heavy rain caused street flooding to occur in Austin. Interstate 90 had to be closed because of the flooding between Oakland Ave NW and 6th Ave NE. One person had to be rescued after driving into flood waters and the car became stuck.

Heavy rain caused Sugar Creek to flood with water going over County Highway 8 west of Fountain. Flooding on Duschee Creek caused State Highway 16 to be closed southwest of Lanesboro. State Highway 16 was also closed west of Whalan due to a mudslide. Downed trees blocked U.S. Highway 52 south of Chatfield and State Highway 43 near Rushford. Ox Cart Road suffered severe damage from a mudslide. Flood waters completely covered Riverside Campground and 70 campers had to be evacuated from the Highway 250 Campground. Numerous township roads were also damaged by the flooding.
Runoff from heavy rains caused water to go over several roads across the southern sections of Dodge County.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding to occur across much of Vernon County. One person was killed near Victory when a mudslide caused a home to slide down a hillside very early in the morning of the 22nd. Numerous other houses were damaged by rocks, debris and floodwaters in Victory when a culvert used to divert water around town became blocked. In and around De Soto, two people had to be rescued from flood waters and 15 people were evacuated from a trailer park. The flood waters also covered State Highway 35. Flooding along Coe Hollow Creek prompted officials to evacuate Sidie Hollow Park but not before one person had to be rescued. Flood waters from the Kickapoo River flooded the west side of La Farge and caused State Highway 131 to be closed both north and south of town. Flooding from the Kickapoo River also sent water spilling into Viola and Readstown. State Highway 82 was closed west of La Farge because of flood waters from Otter Creek. Street flooding occurred in Viroqua where the water was up to 4 feet deep on Main Street. A state of emergency was declared in the county and there were up to 90 roads closed due to flooding. All together, there were a total of 44 homes and businesses destroyed.
Heavy rain caused flooding to occur in the Bluffton area along the Upper Iowa River and Pine and Silver Creeks. Street flooding occurred in Decorah.

Flooding along a branch of Camp Creek sent three feet of water into a house east of Viola. Flooding along Fancy and Marshall Creeks caused roads to be closed near Gillingham. State Highway 56 was closed east of Viola due to flooding along Camp Creek and County Highway C was closed near Yuba because of flooding along the Pine River. A total of 3 homes were destroyed by the flooding with another 72 damaged.
A tornado briefly touched down southeast of Lime Springs with little to no damage reported.

A train derailment occurred near Ferryville when flood waters washed out the roadbed. Around 1,000 gallons of diesel fuel leaked out of one locomotive into the water. Runoff from heavy rains also washed out a portion of State Highway 35 south of Lynxville. A mudslide covered a portion of State Highways 35/82 south of De Soto. A mudslide northeast of Wauzeka sent a large boulder onto State Highway 60. State Highway 35 was closed between De Soto and Prairie du Chien due to flooding and mudslides. Roads were damaged across much of the county with the most damage occurring in the townships of Freeman, Utica, Clayton and Haney. Freeman was hit the hardest with every township road sustaining major damage. A large portion of Rush Creek Road north of Ferryville was washed out. The flooding also caused a large hole to form in State Highway 171 near Gays Mills. Two private structures were destroyed and another 67 damaged by the flooding.
Flooding along the Root River washed out roads just outside of Lanesboro. State Highway 16 was closed southwest of Lanesboro because of a mudslide.
Runoff from heavy rains caused water to cover the roads in Carpenter. Water was also over roads near Stacyville.
Flood waters from Crane Creek covered U.S. Highway 18 northeast of Hawkeye and the streets were flooded in Hawkeye. Numerous roads between West Union and Sumner had water over them.

The fire department had to pump water out of basements in Nashua and volunteers helped sandbag homes in both Nashua and Ionia. Flood waters from the Wapsipinicon River covered U.S. Highway 18 west of New Hampton. For the second time this month, school was canceled in the New Hampton school district because of flooding.

The most damage occurred in McGregor with two buildings downtown completely destroyed while numerous others were damaged. Two people sustained minor injuries due to flying glass. Hundreds of trees across town were snapped off. West of McGregor, the tornado damaged a storage shed, ripped back part of a metal roof from an outbuilding and damaged numerous trees. One person was killed in an accident cleaning up debris when a tractor rolled over pinning the person underneath it.

Heavy rains of 6 to 8 inches across the southern half of Buffalo County produced flash flooding. A mudslide covered a portion of State Highway 37 north of Alma. Portions of County Road O were completely covered by water and the road was closed between Cochrane and State Highway 88. Numerous streets were covered by standing water in Fountain City. Around a half dozen roads were closed across the county because of the flooding.
Power lines were blown down in Alma.

Heavy rains, with totals of 6 to 8 inches, produced flash flooding across the southern sections of Trempealeau County. Arcadia was hit the hardest by the flash flooding. Water rescues had to be performed and all roads in and out of the city were closed due to flood waters. Oak Street was washed out and the water flooded dozens of homes and businesses. One manufacturing plant was destroyed by the flooding and a basement wall of one home collapsed. The manufacturing company lost over $1.5 million because of lost production. State Highway 95 was closed between Arcadia and the Jackson County line because of flooding along Turton and Lakes Coulee Creeks and the Trempealeau River. In Galesville, business along Tamarack Creek were inundated by flood water, including the fire station. The swing bridge over the creek was washed away. Numerous roads were covered by 1 to 2 feet of water including portions of U.S. Highway 53, State Highway 93 and County Roads D and T. At least 15 roads across the county were closed because of the flooding.

Heavy rains, with totals of 6 to 8 inches, produced flash flooding across La Crosse County. The Shelby Fire Department had to evacuate people along County Road M in the township of Greenfield. Some of these evacuations had to be made by boat. Other rescues had to be made along Kammell Coulee Road southeast of St. Joseph. County Road U was closed between Bangor and Rockland due to flooding along Fish Creek. Flood waters along Mormon Creek washed out the approaches to both sides of a bridge on Breidel Coulee Road south of Barre Mills. Some streets in Onalaska were washed out or completely underwater. Numerous streets in the city of La Crosse were underwater causing a giant sinkhole to form near Myrick Park. Every state and county highway, with the exception of Interstate 90 and U.S. Highway 53, sustained some damage. At least 60 township roads across the county were closed or impacted by flood waters. In Bangor, flood waters from Dutch Creek washed away the pedestrian walking bridge in Veterans Memorial Park. Boats on Lake Neshonoc broke loose from their moorings and became lodged against the dam. All the trails in the Hixton Forest suffered erosion damage that caused holes and blowouts to form. The damage to the trails caused a mountain bike race course to be limited to trails that stayed on top of the bluffs. A bike trail along Halfway Creek near Holmen was washed out in several places with other damage caused by logjams and debris in the water.

Heavy rains, with totals of 6 to 8 inches, produced flash flooding across the central and eastern sections of Vernon County. The headwaters of the Kickapoo River quickly went out of the banks and caused widespread flooding in Ontario. Much of the town was covered in flood waters that prompted State Highways 33 and 131 to be closed. Evacuations were performed east of Westby along Bloomingdale Road, which was closed because of flooding. A mudslide east of Viroqua covered State Highway 56. A rock slide occurred on Mohawk Valley Road north of Stoddard. Water covered County Road P and Spring Coulee Road northeast of Coon Valley and State Highway 162 between Coon Valley and Stoddard. Because of the flooding, campers were evacuated from numerous campgrounds across the county.

Heavy rains, with totals of 6 to 8 inches, produced flash flooding across the western and central sections of Monroe County. A mudslide occurred between Sparta and Tomah in the Jackson Pass area that blocked State Highway 16. In Sparta, water spilled over the dam at Perch Lake prompting officials to advise people who lived downstream along the La Crosse River to evacuate, including a trailer park and water went over several roads. Around 10 roads across the county were closed because of the flooding.

Heavy rains, with totals of 6 to 8 inches, produced flash flooding across the central and eastern sections of Richland County. The heavy rains caused the Pine River to go out of its banks which prompted sandbagging to occur in Yuba, closed State Highway 80 at County Road D and caused flooding to occur in Richland Center.

After the initial flash flooding across Trempealeau County, the flood waters continued to cause problems through July 20th into the 21st. Flooding along the Little Tamarack Creek caused evacuations to occur in Galesville and flooded the fire department building. Homes in Galesville and Blair were reported to have 5 to 6 feet of water in some basements. Two homes were destroyed, 12 sustained major damage and 52 suffered minor damage during the flooding.

After the initial flash flooding across Buffalo County, the flood waters continued to cause problems through July 20th into the 21st. Flood waters along Eagle Creek washed out a bridge on County Road G north of Fountain City.

After the initial flash flooding across Richland County, the flooding continued to cause problems through July 20th into the 21st. The flooding along the Pine River prompted an apartment complex to be evacuated and a shelter to be opened in Richland Center. Over a dozen roads were closed across the county because of the flooding. Nine homes sustained minor damage during the flooding.

Locally heavy rains of 4 to 8 inches, produced flash flooding across the southern half of Grant County. Parts of State Highway 81 north of Cassville were washed out where a sinkhole formed. The flood waters around Cassville caused five people to be trapped in their residences and swept away three cars. About a dozen homes had water over the first floor and one home was a complete loss as the flood waters shifted it off the foundation. A person had to be rescued from a floating camper at a campground southeast of Cassville. Around 20 roads were closed or significantly damaged throughout the county because of the flooding. Across the county, a total of 5 homes were destroyed, 12 sustained major damage and 20 had minor damage. In Platteville, numerous streets were flooded with lots of houses surrounded by water and some basements were flooded.

After heavy rains of 4 to 8 inches, flash flooding occurred across the southern half of Clayton County. Flooding along Roberts and Dry Mill Creeks washed out County Road C1X east of Elkader. Numerous other roads were closed across the county due to inundation, rock slides and mud slides with the hardest hit part of the county between Garber and Guttenberg. Near Guttenberg, the residents of three homes had to be rescued from flood waters on Miners Creek. The flooding heavily damaged a bridge over Miners Creek, took out a 30 foot retaining wall, damaged the inventory of two business and undercut railroad tracks.

Heavy rains of 4 to 8 inches caused flash flooding to occur across the southern sections of Chickasaw County. Flood waters from two small creeks covered U.S. Highway 18 west of Fredericksburg. The flood waters prompted sandbagging to be done in New Hampton. Numerous roads across the county sustained damage during the flooding.
In Guttenberg, 7.44 inches of rain fell.

After heavy rains dropped 4 to 8 inches of rain, flash flooding occurred across the southern sections of Fayette County. East of Wadena, the bridge over the Volga River on Acorn Road failed. Otter Creek went out if its banks in Oelwein.
Near Volga, 5.15 inches of rain fell.
West of Ionia, 8.39 inches of rain fell.
Near Fayette, 7.67 inches of rain fell.

After heavy rains of 4 to 8 inches, flash flooding occurred across the southeast half of Floyd County. A road was partially washed out and a railroad crossing was partially washed out southeast of Charles City.
In New Hampton, 8.35 inches of rain fell.
Locally heavy rains pushed the Little Wapsipinicon River and small creeks that feed the river out of their banks. These flood waters covered roads northwest of Westgate.

After the initial flash flooding, the flood waters lingered across much of Fayette County into Sunday, July 23rd. On Saturday morning, numerous roads were reported to be impassable in Fairbank because of the flood waters. Sandbagging was occurring around several businesses. State Highway 3 was closed between Oelwein and Oran. In the town of Fayette, around 80 percent of the homes had water in their basements and a park in town was closed because of the flooding.
Near Burton, 7.20 inches of rain fell.

Runoff from locally heavy rains pushed Coon Creek out of its banks in and near Chaseburg. The flood waters caused county officials to close State Highway 162 near Chaseburg. The water also went into a park and over a walking path in Coon Valley.

After heavy rains of 4 to 6 inches, flash flooding occurred across the southwest sections of Jackson County. French Creek went out of its banks sending water over County Road X southeast of Taylor. The townships of Springfield, Franklin and North Bend were hit the hardest with several roads either washed out or damaged from the flooding. Two homes sustained minor damage during the flooding.

After the initial round of flash flooding, the flood waters continued to cause problems across much of Vernon County into Friday, July 21st. More than 50 roads across the county were closed or impacted by the flood waters. In Coon Valley, the annual Trout Festival had to be cancelled and the American Legion Baseball tournament was moved to an alternate site outside of the county. Numerous homes in Westby had water in their basements. In Ontario, flood waters from the Kickapoo River covered most of the community. Numerous homes had water in their basements and dozens of cars were inundated by the flood waters with one Vernon County Sheriff's Department squad car destroyed.

After the initial round of flash flooding, the lingering flood waters continued to cause problems across Monroe County into Friday, July 21st. Thirty-nine families across the county had to be evacuated and another 56 were affected by the flooding. State Highway 131 in the far southern part of the county was closed because of flooding along the Kickapoo River and State Highway 27 between Leon and Sparta was also closed. Several township roads were flooded along the La Crosse and Baraboo Rivers. A total of 10 state or county highways were closed because of the flooding.  One home sustained major damage and another eight suffered minor damage.
A farmer sustained injuries when the barn he was doing chores in was blown down on top of him.
Trees were blown over on the south side of La Crosse. One of the trees blocked South Avenue near the Shelby Mall while others landed on vehicles. Part of a roof was caved in on a building.

A barn was blown down near Bloomington.

Runoff from heavy rain caused flooding to occur over the eastern portions of Crawford County, especially along the Kickapoo River. This flooding closed State Highway 131 near Stueben and State Highway 171 near Gays Mills. The flooding waters in Stueben lifted asphalt up and off the road bed. Across the northeast part of the county, numerous bridge approaches were damaged by flood waters. Two homes in the county sustained major damage from the flooding with another two having minor damage.
The catholic church in New Haven sustained wind damage.
On a farm near Carpenter, tin silos were  twisted and large trees were blown down. On another farm, a downed tree fell on a house.
A lightning strike started an apartment building fire just west of Galesville. Six apartment units were a total loss as a result of the fire.

Seven people were injured and transported to the hospital when a chartered school bus rolled over southeast of Rochester because of icy roads. The bus fishtailed around a corner, went into the ditch and rolled over. A period of very light freezing rain coated untreated roads with a thin layer of ice. The automated weather observing equipment at the Rochester airport reported light freezing rain for almost three hours.

Two people were transported to the hospital after being injured in separate crashes along Interstate 90 across southern Winona County. The crashes resulted from icy roads after a period of light freezing rain coated untreated roads.

One person was killed in a two vehicle accident near Dresbach on Interstate 90. The driver of one of the vehicles lost control while attempting to pass a semi truck with limited visibility.  The vehicle went through the median, rolled down an embankment, and came to rest on its roof. Heavy rain across the northern portion of Vernon County produced significant flash flooding. Over 200 people were evacuated in Coon Valley because of severe flooding along Coon Creek where U.S. Highway 14 and State Highway 162 were closed. All access into Coon Valley was cut off because of mudslides, washouts and closed roads. Numerous homes were severely damaged with basement walls blown out or had water several feet deep on the first floor. Much of Ontario was covered in flood waters from the Kickapoo River and Brush Creek with almost every business along Garden Street, State Highway 131 and the east end of Main Street sustaining damage. It was estimated that around 75% of the businesses in the entire village sustained some damage. The Ontario police squad car become submerged in flood waters and was destroyed. One boat rental business lost 40 canoes and 48 kayaks. Two campers along the Kickapoo River north of Rockton had to be rescued from flood waters that was neck high. Some residents were evacuated from Viola because of flooding along the Kickapoo River. A total of 350 water rescues were performed across the county. State Highway 131 was closed between Ontario and Rockton because of flood waters from the Kickapoo River where the asphalt was completely removed from the road bed in places or broken in large chunks and then moved up to eight feet from its original location. Numerous roads were closed because of the flooding or from mudslides. Flooding from Timber Coulee Creek washed out over 20 power poles north of Westby. The BNSF rail line was closed because of washouts between Stoddard and the La Crosse County line. The heavy rain and flooding caused two earthen flood control dams to fail and damaged four others.  This prompted the evacuation and rescue of residents downstream from the dams, including the communities of Avalanche and Liberty. Wildcat Mountain State Park was closed because of the heavy rain as well.

Runoff from heavy rain caused flash flooding across the southern portions of La Crosse County. Homes were evacuated and roads closed along State Highway 35 south of La Crosse and County Road K near Goose Island Park. Flood waters from Mormon Creek were chest high in a mobile home part along U.S. Highways 14/61 southeast of La Crosse where water rescues had to be performed. The BNSF rail line was closed because of washouts between La Crosse and the Vernon County line. Sections of Highways 14/61 in the southern end of the county were damaged and had mudslides over them.

Runoff from heavy rain caused flash flooding to occur across the southern sections of Monroe County. Near Melvina, a resident had to be rescued from a home surrounded by flood waters. Flooding was extreme along the Little La Crosse River along and just east of Highway 27 between Cashton and Sparta where numerous homes were flooded, rescues were needed, and roads were damaged.  Flooding along Moore Creek in Norwalk damaged some ballfields and the village office. In Kendall, a park along the Baraboo River was destroyed and a newly installed road to the village's wastewater treatment plant was washed out. Most of the flood damaged homes and business were along Glen Street. Across the county, 75 people had to be evacuated. At the Skogdalen cemetery, 90% of the gravestones markers were toppled, debris was up to 5 feet deep in places and ripped apart the road in front of the church. Numerous roads were closed, with most of these in the far southern part of the county in Portland, Jefferson, Sheldon, Wellington and Glendale Townships. Some of the impacted roads included: County Highway N, County Highway Z south of Wilton, County Highway P near Kendall, County Highway F south of Norwalk, County Highway D near Cashton, County Highway CM near Tomah, State Highway 33 east of Cashton, County Highway W north of Kendall, County Highway ET east of Tomah and County Highway F east of Melvina. The heavy rain and flooding caused three earthen flood control dams to fail and damaged three others.

Runoff from heavy rain caused extensive flooding to occur in Elroy from the Baraboo River. Between 25 and 30 homes had to be evacuated. Numerous homes had water several inches to a few feet deep in the basements. Nine homes likely will have to be torn down. Damages in Elroy totaled nearly $6.5 million. The flooding along the Baraboo River also hit Wonewoc hard causing officials to evacuate the western half of the town. Dozens of homes had water in the basements with at least 4 of them suffering collapsed walls. Flooding along the Lemonweir River near Mauston caused Interstates 90/94 to be closed in both directions and washed out a rail line that caused the eastbound Amtrak Empire Builder to be stopped near Tomah. Passengers had to remain on the stopped train overnight until repairs to the rail line were completed. Flooding in Mauston damaged some homes with at least one a total loss when a basement wall collapsed. Flood waters from Webster Creek covered portions of State Highway 80 between New Lisbon and Elroy. State Highway 33 was under water in places between Union Center and Wonewoc because of flood waters from the Baraboo River. State Highway 82 was closed between Elroy and Mauston due to flood waters from Cleaver Creek. Portions of State Highway 58 south of Mauston was covered in flood waters from Onemile and Stewart Creeks. U.S. Highway 12 was closed between Mauston and Lyndon Station because of flooding on the Lemonweir River. County highways across the southern part of the county that were closed included: N, G, HH and FF. Numerous local and township roads were also closed.

Light to moderate snow fell across Winona County from March 9th into the 10th with accumulations of 2 to 3 inches. The weight of this snow, along with the copious amounts that fell in February, caused the roof over a hotel pool and part of a factory roof to collapse in Winona.

Light to moderate snow fell across Buffalo County from March 9th into the 10th with accumulations generally in the 3 to 4 inch range. The weight of this snow, combined with the copious amounts that fell in February, caused the roof over a large hog barn near Mondovi to collapse. A fire that started after the roof collapsed killed almost 4,000 hogs.

An elderly woman drowned in Mississippi River flood waters in the vicinity of Blackhawk Park.  Sometime during the night of March 29th into the early morning hours of March 30th, the woman wandered away from her home and was swept away by flood waters.

At least three county roads were closed because of downed power lines. A countywide state of emergency was declared with shelters opened for those without power.

Runoff from rain and snowmelt pushed the Trempealeau River out of its banks in Dodge. The river crested around a foot and a half above the flood stage at 10.62 feet on April 20th.
Runoff from rain and melting snow pushed the Black River out of its banks in Neillsville. The river crested around a half foot above the flood stage at 18.42 feet on April 18th.
Runoff from rain and melting snow pushed the Black River out of its banks near Hatfield. The river crested over four feet above the flood stage at 801.33 feet on April 18th.
Runoff from rain and snowmelt pushed the Black River out of its banks in Black River Falls. The river crested just over eleven feet above the flood stage at 58.04 feet on April 18th.
Runoff from rain and snowmelt pushed the Black River out of its banks near Galesville. The river crested almost three feet above the flood stage at 14.95 feet on April 19th.
Runoff from rain and snowmelt pushed the Yellow River out of its banks in Necedah. The river crested over three feet above the flood stage at 18.77 feet on April 20th.
Runoff from rain and melting snow produced high flows through the Castle Rock Dam. The flow topped out at 52,861 cubic feet per second (cfs) on April 19th. Flood stage is considered 30,000 cfs.
Runoff from rain and melting snow pushed the Wisconsin River out of its banks in Muscoda. The river crested around a half foot above the flood stage at 9.55 feet on April 24th.

Flooding that began in late March along the Mississippi River in Lake City, continued into the middle of April. The river crested about a foot and a half above the flood stage at 17.63 feet on April 1st.

Flooding that began in late March along the Mississippi River in Wabasha, continued through the entire month of April. The river first crested around three and half feet above the flood stage on April 1st. The river crested a second time just over three feet above the flood stage on April 22nd.

Flooding that began in late March along the Mississippi River in Winona, continue through the entire month of April. The river first crested over four feet above the flood stage at 17.3 feet on April 2nd. The river crested a second time about three and a half feet above the flood stage at 16.88 feet on April 23rd.

Flooding that began in late March along the Mississippi River in La Crosse, continued through the entire month of April. The river first crested around two and half feet above the flood stage at 14.58 feet on April 2nd. The river crested a second time over two feet above the flood stage at 14.33 feet on April 23rd. Numerous parks, boat landings, campgrounds and some roads were closed because of the flooding.
High flows along the Mississippi River caused flooding to occur in Lansing during the early part of April. The river crested just under a foot above the flood stage at 17.89 feet on April 4th.

Flooding that began in late March along the Mississippi River in McGregor continued through the entire month of April. The river first crested over five feet above the flood stage at 21.34 feet on April 4th. The river crested a second time almost six feet over the flood stage at 21.75 feet on April 26th.

Flooding that began in late March on the Mississippi River in Guttenberg continued through the entire month of April. The river first crested over four feet above the flood stage at 19.59 feet on April 5th. The river crested a second time almost five feet above the flood stage at 19.98 feet on April 27th.

A second round of runoff from rain and snowmelt caused renewed flooding to occur along the Mississippi River in Lake City. The river crested just under a foot above the flood stage at 16.88 feet on April 22nd.

A second round of runoff from rain and snowmelt caused renewed flooding to occur along the Mississippi River in Lansing. The river crested just under a foot above the flood stage at 17.83 feet on April 26th.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that between 2 and 4 inches of snow fell across Houston County. In addition to the snow, a period of sleet and freezing rain occurred that coated exposed surfaces with a glaze of ice. With the glaze of ice, some power poles and lines were brought down by the strong winds causing about a 3,000 people to lose power.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that between 4 and 7 inches of snow fell across La Crosse County. In addition to the snow, a period of sleet and freezing rain occurred that coated exposed surfaces with a glaze of ice. With the glaze of ice, some power poles and lines were brought down by the strong winds causing about a 1,000 people to lose power. A lightning strike hit and destroyed a tree in West Salem.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that between 5 and 6 inches of snow fell across Fillmore County. In addition to the snow, a period of sleet and freezing rain occurred that coated exposed surfaces with a glaze of ice. With the glaze of ice, some power poles and lines were brought down by the strong winds causing the entire town of Rushford to lose power.

Strong east winds from an early spring storm gusted has high as 61 mph near West Union. The strong winds flipped a semi onto its side north of West Union causing State Highway 150 to be closed for almost two hours. Trees and power lines were also downed by the winds.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that between 3 and 5 inches of snow fell across Monroe County. In addition to the snow, a period of sleet and freezing rain occurred that coated exposed surfaces with a glaze of ice. A home near Sparta was severely damaged by a fire started from a lightning strike.
Quarter sized hail fell in Elkader.

Heavy rainfall of 3 to 5 inches caused flash flooding to occur in and near New Hampton. There were many reports of high water in town with numerous streets and intersections under water along with water in basements. Sandbagging was performed in some parts of town. The flood waters also covered U.S. Highway 63 north of town.
In New Hampton, 4.54 inches of rain fell.

A tornado touched down west of Charles City and moved north-northeast before dissipating northwest of Colwell. The tornado did extensive damage to seven buildings at the Floyd County fairgrounds. At a fertilizer plant across the road from the fairgrounds a roof was partially peeled off from one building while the main building was left leaning after having an entire side ripped off.  Three homes along the path were damaged severely enough to be declared inhabitable.

A tornado touched down across northwest Chickasaw County southwest of Alta Vista. The tornado traveled north-northeast across rural parts of the county before passing into Howard County southwest of Elma. This was spotted by area fire departments.

A tornado entered into Howard County southwest of Elma as it moved north-northeast and then dissipated after crossing Dale Avenue. Farm buildings were damaged just north of the Chickasaw County line. This was witnessed by area fire departments serving as spotters.

A tornado formed over rural Howard County south of Saratoga and then traveled north-northeast before dissipating just before entering Lime Springs. The tornado struck and destroyed a wind turbine north of State Highway 9 and also destroyed a large farm building along Lilac Avenue.

A tornado formed over far northern Howard County north of Lime Springs before quickly moving across the state line into Fillmore County, Minnesota. This was the third tornado of the day in Howard County.

A tornado that developed just south of the Minnesota state line moved into Fillmore County south of York and then moved north-northeast before dissipating near Greenleafton. A small barn and machine shed was destroyed and another sustained roof damage from the tornado. Another two farms also sustained some minor damage to buildings and a few homes sustained minor wind and tree damage.
A brief tornado touched down in rural southwest Fillmore County south of Ostrander. The tornado flipped a farm shed over a tree line.
A tornado briefly touched down near Etna and uprooted some trees at a cemetery.
A tornado briefly touched down east of Spring Valley. A cattle barn was heavily damaged just north of County Highway 16.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Whitewater River out of its banks in Whitewater River State Park. The river crested a foot above the flood stage at 14.54 feet.
Flooding along the Mississippi River at Wabasha that began in March, temporarily ended in early May.
Flooding along the Mississippi River at Winona that began in March, temporarily ended in early May.
Flooding along the Mississippi River at La Crosse that began in March, temporarily ended in early May.
Flooding along the Mississippi River at McGregor that began in March, temporarily ended in late May.
Flooding along the Mississippi River at Guttenberg that began in March, temporarily ended in late May.

Runoff from a couple of rainfall events pushed the Mississippi River out of its banks again in Wabasha. The river crested almost two feet above the flood stage at 13.89 feet on May 24th and had a second crest of 13.69 feet on May 31st. The flooding continued into June.

Runoff after a couple of rainfall events pushed the Mississippi River out of its banks again in Winona. The river crested over two feet above the flood stage at 15.13 feet on May 25th. The flooding continued into June.

Runoff after a couple of rain events pushed the Mississippi River out of its banks again in La Crosse. The river crested over a foot above the flood stage at 13.24 feet on May 25th. The flooding continued into June.

Runoff after a couple of rainfall events pushed the Mississippi River out of its banks again in McGregor. The river crested over three feet above the flood stage at 19.09 feet on May 30th. The flooding continued into June.

Runoff after a couple of rainfall events pushed the Mississippi River out of its banks again in Guttenberg. The river crested around two and a half feet above the flood stage at 17.56 feet on May 31st. The flooding continued into June.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Turkey River out of its banks in Spillville. The river crested less than a half foot above the flood stage at 9.13 feet.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Turkey River out of its banks in Elkader. The river crested less than a half foot above the flood stage at 12.23 feet.

After a tornado dissipated just outside of Lime Springs, the remaining winds from the storm blew down several trees and powerlines and cause some roof damage to homes in town. Around 900 residents were without power after the storm.
Trees were damaged when a brief tornado crossed Highways 14/61 between La Crosse and Coon Valley.

An estimated 60 mph wind gust occurred in the Apache Mall area in Rochester. Numerous trees and power lines were blown down across the southwest part of the city. At one point, up to 2,000 customers were without power.

Runoff from heavy rain produced flash flooding across the eastern portions of Mower County. The intersection of U.S. Highway 63 and State Highway 16 was covered in water and both Deer Creek and Bear Creek went out of their banks.

Runoff from heavy rain produced some flash flooding across the western portions of Fillmore County. Water covered roads west of Spring Valley and several small creeks went out of their banks including Spring Valley, Little Kingsley, Deer and Bear. In the city of Spring Valley, water from Spring Valley creek flooded the downtown area for the first time in more than a decade. At least three people tried to drive their vehicles through the flood waters with all three vehicles becoming stranded. Two of the people needed assistance from the Spring Valley fire department to be safely removed from the flood waters. Near Ostrander, water went over County Road 14 and deposited debris from a farm field that made travel difficult after the water receded.
An estimated 5.75 inches of rain fell in Spring Valley.
Runoff from locally heavy rain caused a couple of small mudslides to occur along State Highway 162 near Koll Lane east of Stoddard.
Northeast of Stoddard, 3.3 inches of rain fell.
Just south of Stoddard, 3.47 inches of rain fell.
Quarter sized hail fell northeast of Elma.
Nickel sized hail fell in Elma.
Large tree branches were blown down in Charles City.
Trees and power lines were blown down in the city of La Crosse. A boat (of unknown size) was flipped over on French Island.
Trees were blown down in and just north of Sparta, which caused some power outages.
A large tree was blown down in Viroqua.
Trees were blown down in Strawberry Point.
Trees were blown down west of Elkader along State Highway 56.
A large tree branch and several smaller branches were blown down in West Salem.

Quarter sized hail fell just west of Lake City.

Flash flooding occurred across the western sections of Olmsted County after thunderstorms dropped 3 to 7 inches of rain. The Rochester International airport was closed after water covered the runways. Along the South Branch of the Middle Fork of the Zumbro River, between 40 and 60 cows were swept away north of Byron with about 15 of these cows drowning. The campground at Oxbow County Park was flooded with the water damaging at least one car. U.S. Highways 52 and 63 and numerous other roads had water over them. Some business on the southwest side of Rochester suffered water damage when flood waters entered the buildings.

Thunderstorms with very heavy rain dumped between 3 and 7 inches across much of Dodge County. Flash flooding resulted from this rain with water covering numerous roads, including U.S. Highway 14. Near Wasioja, 605th Street was washed out. A truck tried to drive through flood waters on State Highway 56 and was swept into a nearby field. The occupants of the truck were not injured.

Thunderstorms with heavy rain dropped 3 to 5 inches of rain across the northwest portions of Fillmore County. This caused some flash flooding to occur, which was mainly water going over roads. Water from Mill Creek flooded a park in the southwest side of Chatfield and went over County Road 2.
After the heavy rain earlier in the day, flooding continued across portions of Dodge County. Flood waters from Masten Creek covered State Highway 57 in Kasson.

In Claremont, 5.69 inches of rain fell.

A few residences along Rongholt Valley Road and County Road Z sustained wind damage from passing thunderstorms, including damage to trees and smaller buildings.

Trees were blown down south of Davis Corners and a roof was blown off of a unknown building type.

Lots of trees were blown down across the entire county.

A tree, between 12 and 24 inches in diameter, was snapped off east of Oelwein.
The automated weather observing equipment at the Platteville airport measured a gust of 75 mph.

Lots of trees and power lines were blown down across much of Grant County. The hardest hit areas were across the southern half of the county, including Cuba City which was hit particularly hard with damaging winds. 20,000 customers across the county were without power.
A large metal building sustained severe roof damage near Randalia. Boards from the damaged building were driven into a nearby shed.
A home southeast of Coon Valley was struck by lightning with the resulting fire destroying the entire structure.
A lightning strike started a house fire southeast of La Crosse. The home sustained significant damage to one corner.
A lightning strike started a small house fire in La Crosse. The fire damage was limited to the basement.
A lightning strike from a thunderstorm struck a parked boat near Lake Camelot east of Rome. The resulting fire destroyed the boat and damaged some trees.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Whitewater River out of its banks in the Whitewater State Park. The river crested a half foot above the flood stage at 13.98 feet.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the South Fork of the Zumbro River out of its banks in Rochester. The river crested over two and a half feet above the flood stage at 16.57 feet on June 28th.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Zumbro River out of its banks in Zumbro Falls. The river crested just over nine feet above the flood stage at 27.03 feet on June 29th.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Upper Iowa River out of its banks near Dorchester. The river crested around a half foot above the flood stage at 14.6 feet.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Turkey River out of its banks in Spillville. The river crested almost two feet above the flood stage at 10.82 feet.

Runoff from heavy rains pushed Cascade Creek out of its banks in Rochester. The creek crested over a foot above the flood stage at 14.21 feet.
Trees were blown down east of Altura.
Wind gusts were estimated at 59 mph along Interstate 90 southeast of St.Charles.
A couple of trees were knocked down on rural roads between Nashua and New Hampton.
A few trees were blown down along 770th Ave.

Slow moving thunderstorms dropped between 3 and 5 inches of rain across the northeast portion of Grant County. Runoff from the rain caused a mudslide to occur along County Highway M south of Blue River and water covered County Highway B southeast of Ellenboro. A mudslide near Glen Haven covered some railroad tracks resulting in a train derailment. Nine cars derailed with one partially going into the Mississippi River.
After thunderstorms dropped between 2 and 5 inches of rain across much of Grant County, several rivers and streams flooded including the Little Platte, Platte and Grant rivers.
In Platteville, 3.7 inches of rain fell.
The automated weather observing equipment at the Boscobel airport measured 2.61 inches of rain.
Water covered roads in and around Dodge Center after slow moving thunderstorms dropped between 2 and 6 inches of rain. Several roads had to be closed until the water receded.
Water covered roads in and near Byron after thunderstorms dropped between 2 and 6 inches of rain. U.S. Highway 14 was closed in Byron after water covered all the lanes of traffic.
In Kasson, 4.8 inches of rain fell.
Near Kasson, 6.8 inches of rain fell.
In Byron, 6.7 inches of rain fell.
Quarter sized hail fell between Woodman and Boscobel.
An estimated 60 mph wind gust occurred near Mindoro.
An estimated 60 mph wind gust occurred near Tomah.
The northbound lane of County Highway YY was blocked east of Barre Mills when trees were blown down.

Runoff from heavy rain caused mudslides to occur south of Pickwick. The mudslide took down trees and covered County Road 7 between Pickwick and County Road 12. County Road 7 was also covered by floodwaters from Big Trout Creek. A rockslide occurred on Garvin Heights Road in the city of Winona.

Runoff from heavy rains caused flash flooding to occur along the Kickapoo River and Coon Creek. Campers had to be evacuated from the Kickapoo Valley Reserve. County Road P was covered by a mudslide and flood waters east of Westby. Flood waters also covered County Road P north of Coon Valley. U.S. Highway 14 was closed near Coon Valley when water from Coon Creek covered the road. State Highway 162 from Coon Valley through Chaseburg was closed along with State Highway 56 near Liberty. A bridge was washed out on Spring Coulee Road east of Coon Valley.

Southeast of Westby, four inches of rain fell.
Near Ridgeway, between 4.5 and 5 inches of rain fell.
South of Winona, 4.54 inches of rain fell.
East of Westby, 5.74 inches of rain fell.
A brief tornado touched down northeast of Westby. A barn was destroyed, a trailer flipped and numerous trees damaged.
Sporadic wind damage occurred along State Highway 33 west of Cashton.
A wind gust of 61 mph was measured by a private weather station southwest of Stetsonville.
Numerous tree branches were blown down and the power was knocked out in Colby.
Some trees were blown down north of Owen. A 50 mph wind gust was measured by a private weather station.
Trees and power lines were blown down in Abbotsford and Colby. Additional power lines were downed along State Highway 13 north of Abbotsford.
West of Withee, two barns, a garage and silo were blown down.
A barn and garage were both damaged east of Thorp.
The automated weather observing equipment at the Rochester International Airport measured a wind gust of 74 mph.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down across the northern part of La Crosse County.
Trees were blown down in various places across the western part of the county.
Trees were blown down along County Highway Q northeast of Sparta near Angelo.
A semi-truck was blown off U.S. Highway 10 near Neillsville.
Rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches were common across the eastern portions of Dodge County. Runoff from this rain caused a pond west of Mantorville to overflow its dam.
A 61 mph wind gust occurred at Fort McCoy. Shingles were blown off some buildings.
Several trees and power lines were blown down north of Blair.

Rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches were common across the northwest part of Olmsted County. Runoff from this rain caused water to go over several rural roads. Oxbow Park and Zollman Zoo had to be closed because of flood waters from the South Branch of the Middle Fork Zumbro River.
Numerous trees were blown down in Austin.
Trees were blown down in Winona.

Two injuries occurred as severe storms with damaging winds rolled across the southern sections of Trempealeau County. In Galesville, one person was injured by flying glass. Another person was injured when a tree fell on a camper in the Township of Gale. Several buildings were damaged and numerous trees were blown down by the damaging winds.

A brief tornado occurred in the far southeast corner of Trempealeau County southeast of Ettrick. The tornado touched down in a corn field, crossed State Highway 54 and dissipated in a wooden area. Damage was limited to the corn and trees.

A tornado moved across the far southwest corner of Jackson County northeast of North Bend. The tornado touched down in a small wooden area, moved across State Highway 54 before dissipating in another wooded area. Damage was limited to trees and some corn.
On the northwest side of Rochester, a mesonet station measured 2.95 inches of rain.
An estimated 60 mph wind gust blew down trees in Arcadia.

A brief tornado occurred west of Withee. The tornado touched down near a farm where the roof was partially torn off a barn, the top of a silo was ripped off, pole barns were damaged along with between 15 and 20 trees. The tornado then crossed County Highway O before dissipating.

A brief tornado occurred east of Witoka. The tornado touched down on a ridge top and damaged a house and some trees before dissipating before crossing County Road 7.

Runoff from heavy rain caused flash flooding to occur along Coolridge and Rush Creeks in and north of Rushford. Some campers along Coolridge Creek had to evacuate, leaving their vehicles behind, which were severely damaged by the flooding.

Runoff from heavy rains pushed Cascade Creek out of its banks in Rochester. The creek crested almost three feet above the flood stage at 15.76 feet. A water rescue had to be performed in a city park to rescue a man that had been sleeping in the park and became trapped by the rising waters.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed Day Creek out if its banks near Mound Prairie. County Road 21 had to closed because of the flood waters.

A fatal accident occurred during a thunderstorm with heavy rain south of Whitehall. Authorities believe weather was a factor in the head-on two vehicle crash. One person was killed with the other driver sustaining serious injuries.
Multiple trees were blown down at a campground along the Black River southeast of Galesville. Almost all 200 campsites were evacuated as the storms rolled through.

A fire was started by a lightning strike in Genoa. A garage was initially hit with the resulting fire spreading to the house. Both structures were destroyed by the fire. Two off-duty police officers had to rescue a person trapped in burning house.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Yellow River out of its banks in Necedah. The river crested around a foot above the flood stage on the 24th.

Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Whitewater River out of its banks in the Whitewater State Park. The river was above the flood stage for less than hour with a crest almost a foot above the flood stage.
The runoff from a second heavy rain event pushed the Whitewater River out of its banks in the Whitewater state Park. The river crested around a half foot above the flood stage at 13.85 feet.
Runoff from heavy rain pushed the Whitewater River out of its banks in the Whitewater State Park. The river crested over a foot above the flood stage at 14.7 feet.

St.Olaf had about $35,000 in damages, mostly due to erosion.  At least two bridges were washed out in the county.

More than 20 roads were reported closed due to flash flooding. In fact, several roads remained closed, even one week after the heavy rains. There was also damage to bridges and culverts.
