COOP and volunteer snow observers reported 5 to 9 inches of snow across Trempealeau County. The highest reported total was 9 inches in the Village of Trempealeau.
COOP and volunteer snow observers reported 6 to 9 inches of snow across Vernon County. The highest reported total was 9.5 inches in Genoa.

Two people were killed and two more were injured in a single vehicle accident on Interstate 90 near Dexter. Light snow fell during the evening of February 12th followed by northwest winds of 15 to 25 mph into the morning of the 13th. This created some blowing and drifting snow and caused icy conditions to develop on some roads. The driver of the vehicle lost control on an icy spot, went through the median before coming to a stop in the opposite lanes of traffic. The two people killed were thrown from the vehicle.

Wind chill values of 30 to 40 below zero were common across Dodge County during the late evening of the 13th into the morning of the 14th. The coldest recorded wind chill was 41 below at Dodge Center. Some schools across the county used a two hour late start.

Wind chill values of 30 to 40 below were common across Fillmore County during the morning of February 14th. The coldest recorded wind chill was 44 below at a mesonet station near Canton. Some schools across the county used a two hour late start.

Wind chills of 30 to 40 below were common across Mower County during the late evening of February 13th into the morning of the 14th. The coldest recorded wind chill was 40 below at mesonet stations near Dexter and in Austin. Several schools across the county used a two hour late start.

Wind chills of 30 to 40 below zero were common across Olmsted County during the late evening of February 13th into the morning of the 14th. The coldest recorded wind chill was 44 below at Rochester. Several schools across the county used a two hour late start.
Wind chills of 30 to 40 below were common across Winona County during the morning of February 14th. The coldest recorded wind chill was 38 below by a mesonet station near Ridgeway.

One person was killed in a two vehicle accident south of Blooming Prairie on the morning of February 7th. After the collision, one of the vehicles caught on fire. The roads were reported to be snow and ice covered at the time of the accident and the automated weather observing equipment at the Austin and Dodge Center airports were both reporting light snow.

No homes or businesses had major damage due to flood waters, although there were widespread reports of basement flooding in homes. Due to the excessive rainfall, the Turkey River at Eldorado rose 8 feet in 9 hours on the morning of April 25. The Turkey River crested at 18.07 feet at Eldorado, which was only 1.5 feet below the record level of 19.6 feet.

An EF1 tornado moved through the west and northwest side of Oelwein during the late afternoon of March 28th. The tornado produced extensive tree damage at Red Gate Park, blew in the wall of an apartment building and damaged the siding and roof of a second apartment building. The building that sustained the wall damage was condemned. One person was injured at the apartment complex when they stepped on broken glass. At least two vehicles parked outside the apartment complex were heavily damaged.
A funnel cloud was sighted near Fayette. This was likely the remnants of the Maynard tornado.
Quarter sized hail fell in Elkader.
A funnel cloud was sighted in St. Olaf.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Monona.

An EF0 tornado touched down touched down southeast of Maynard and move north-northeast before dissipating between Maynard and Fayette. Several farm buildings were damaged along the path of the tornado.

An EF1 tornado touched down north of Potosi and move northeast for 6 miles before dissipating west of Ellenboro. One house, numerous farm buildings, trees and power lines were damaged along the path of the tornado.
A funnel cloud was sighted southwest of Guttenberg.

Runoff from heavy rainfall caused significant rises on the Turkey River and caused moderate to major flooding. At Elkader, the Turkey River crested at 18.84 feet on April 25. Flood stage is 12 feet.  Damage was estimated at $100,000 including damage to the dike on the town's southwest side and erosion on the riverbank on the northwest side of the community.  At Garber, the river crested at 27.98 feet on April 25, which was below the record setting crest of 32.8 feet on May 23, 2004. Flood stage at Garber is 17 feet.

Runoff from excessive rainfall caused significant flooding of several homes and businesses. In fact, there were approximately 70 homes which suffered damage to flood waters. Some of the locations which were hardest hit included Lancaster, Platteville, Ellenboro, Glenn Haven, Cassville and Potosi. Even a week after the heavy rains, some roads and bridges remained closed due to washouts and effects of debris hitting these structures. In addition, some farm fields remained unusable due to erosion or standing water. Grant County has been hit by major flooding in 2002, 2004, 2007 and 2008.

One person was killed in a single vehicle accident east of Owen on State Highway 29. The driver lost control, the vehicle went into the median and the driver was thrown from the vehicle. Light snow has been falling for most of the afternoon with the roads reported to be slippery at the time of the accident.

One person was killed and another injured when two semi's collided at the intersection of U.S. Highway 52 and State Highway 13 southeast of Monona. The driver of one semi failed to stop at the intersection and collided with the second semi. Lead-acid batteries were strewn across the roads as a result of the accident. A hazard materials team had to be called in for clean up, resulting in the roads being closed for several hours. The visibility was likely reduced to less than a half mile in dense fog at the time of the accident.
Half dollar sized hail was reported in Westboro.
Quarter sized hail fell north of Westboro.
Penny to quarter sized hail was reported in Dickeyville.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that 7 to 9 inches of snow fell across Dodge County. The highest reported total was 9 inches in Mantorville. Strong northwest winds created blowing and drifting snow during the late afternoon and evening hours.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that 5 to 6 inches of snow fell across Mower County. The highest reported total was 6 inches near Lansing. Strong northwest winds created blowing and drifting snow during the late afternoon and evening hours.

One person was killed in a accident when the car they were driving collided with a tow truck parked on the shoulder of U.S. Highway 52 in Rochester. The accident report indicated roads were snow covered at the time of the accident. COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that 4 to 10 inches of snow fell across Olmsted County. The highest reported total was 10 inches north of Viola. Strong northwest winds created blowing and drifting snow during the late afternoon and evening hours.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that 5 to 10 inches of snow fell across Wabasha County. The highest reported total was 10.8 inches near Elgin. Strong northwest winds created blowing and drifting snow during the late afternoon and evening hours.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that 4 to 7 inches of snow fell across Winona County. The highest reported total was 7 inches near Rollingstone. Strong northwest winds created blowing and drifting snow during the late afternoon and evening hours.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that 5 to 9 inches of snow fell across Buffalo County. The highest reported total was 9 inches near Montana. Strong northwest winds created blowing and drifting snow during the late afternoon and evening hours.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that 6 to 11 inches of snow fell across Clark County. The highest reported total was 11 inches near Owen. Strong northwest winds created blowing and drifting snow during the late afternoon and evening hours.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that 6 to 10 inches of snow fell across Taylor County. The highest reported total was 10 inches in Medford. Strong northwest winds created blowing and drifting snow during the late afternoon and evening hours.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that 4 to 7 inches of snow fell across Trempealeau County. The highest reported total was 7 inches in Arcadia and near Independence. Strong northwest winds created blowing and drifting snow during the late afternoon and evening hours.

The driver of a pickup failed to stop for a stop sign at an intersection along U.S. Highway 61 near Potosi, collided with a semi-truck and was thrown from the vehicle. According to the accident report, the driver was pronounced dead at the scene of the accident and that dense fog was a contributing factor. The automated weather observing equipment at the Platteville and Dubuque airports were both reporting dense fog with a visibility of a quarter mile or less at the time of the accident.
Several trees and power lines were blown down across the northern portions of Clark County as a line of thunderstorms moved across the area.
Some trees and power lines were blown down in the Neillsville area.
Runoff from melted snow pushed the Yellow River out of its banks in Necedah. The river crested around a half foot above the flood stage at 15.62 feet on April 1st.
Runoff from melted snow pushed the Mississippi River out of its banks in La Crosse. The river crested over a half foot above the flood stage at 12.67 feet on April 5th.
Runoff from melted snow pushed the Mississippi River out of its banks in Wabasha. The river crested over a foot above the flood stage at 13.3 feet on April 4th.
Runoff from melted snow pushed the Mississippi River out of its banks in Winona. The river crested over a foot above the flood stage at 14.2 feet on April 4th.

Runoff from melted snow pushed the Mississippi River out of its banks in Guttenberg. The river crested almost two feet above the flood stage at 16.76 feet on April 8th.

A wildfire burned around 240 acres of lowland and marsh region in the Necedah Wildlife Refuge on April 18th. Some residents living near the refuge had to be evacuated for safety precautions and State Highway 80 was closed north of Necedah. The remote automated weather station located on the refuge indicated the relative humidity fell to under 25% during the afternoon with southwest winds of 15 to 20 mph gusting up to 39 mph.

An elderly Ettrick man died after sustaining burns trying to put out a grassfire. The fire started as a result of a burning pile of garbage. The automated weather observing equipment at the La Crosse airport indicated the relative humidity was around 35% with a a southwest wind gusting to around 20 mph at the time of the fire.

Runoff from the heavy rains associated with Tropical Depression Cristobal pushed the Turkey River out of its banks twice in Spillville. A home on the south side of La Crosse was damaged when a large tree was uprooted. Numerous other trees were blown down across the city.

The metal siding was ripped off the side of a grain mill southeast of Ontario.
Trees were blown down in Wilton. At least one tree landed on a car, others fell on houses and the roof of a shed was destroyed by a tree that fell on it. Shingles were also blown off a garage.

Runoff from heavy rain pushed Cameron Creek out of its banks northwest of Willard. Flood waters from the creek were reported to be flowing over roads near the intersection of County Highways M and GG.

One person was killed in a single vehicle accident east of Liberty. The accident occurred during a thunderstorm with heavy rain. The driver was believed to have lost control in the heavy rain with the vehicle leaving the road, rolling and ejecting the driver.

A building near Muscoda was destroyed in a fire started by a lightning strike. Isolated thunderstorms moved across southwest Wisconsin during the evening of July 28th. It is believed that lightning hit a nearby pine tree with the resulting fire spreading to the building. The fire was not discovered until the following morning.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused some flash flooding to occur across the southern portions of Adams County. Roads were washed out near Plainville.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported that around 6 inches of snow fell across much of Clark County. The highest reported total was 6 inches near Riplinger, Dorchester and Colby.

An elderly lady wandered away from a senior living center on the southwest side of Rochester during the early morning of October 26th. She was later found in snow a few blocks away from the center after spending a few hours outdoors with air temperatures around 20 and wind chills near 10. The cause of death was likely hypothermia.

Two to three inches of new snow were whipped around by wind gusts of 40 to 45 mph creating a period of blizzard to near blizzard conditions during the late afternoon and evening of December 23rd. The visibility was reduced to a mile or less by blowing snow between 5 and 930 p.m. The highest recorded wind gust by the automated weather observing equipment at the Dodge Center airport was 44 mph.

One to two inches of new snow were whipped around by wind gusts of 40 to 45 mph creating a period of blizzard to near blizzard conditions during the late afternoon and evening of December 23rd. The visibility was reduced to a mile or less by blowing snow between 615 and 815 p.m. The highest recorded wind gust by the automated weather observing equipment at the Austin airport was 44 mph.

One to three inches of new snow were whipped around by wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph creating a period of blizzard to near blizzard conditions during the late afternoon and evening of December 23rd. The visibility was reduced to a mile or less by blowing snow between 630 and 1015 p.m. The highest recorded wind gust by the automated weather observing equipment at the Rochester airport was 50 mph.

A few pine trees were blown down in a campground near Highway 54, but more extensive damage was reported at a cranberry farm where one building was blown down and many nearby trees were broken or sheared off. There may have been a brief gustnado. Cranberry vines were extensively damaged as well.
Hail up to the size of quarters accumulated approximately 8 inches deep. In fact, hail still covered the ground the following morning. Cranberry vines suffered damage due to the large hail.
Penny size hail was reported by students at Luther College to KDEC radio in Decorah.

A western Wisconsin woman died in northern Adams County as a result of hypothermia. Local officials found the woman's car submerged up to the roof in a water filled ditch. The woman escape from the car but with soaking wet clothes and temperatures in the single digits above zero, hypothermia quickly set in and her body was found two days after the accident just a few hundred yards from the car.
Snowfall totals in parts of Fayette County reached 6 inches. Wadena had the most with 6 inches of new snow.

COOP and volunteer snow observers reported 4 to 6 inches of snow across much of Olmsted County. The highest reported total was 6 inches in Rochester. The snow was preceded by a period of freezing rain that created a glaze of ice accumulation on untreated surfaces such as cars and sidewalks.

A northeast Iowa man was killed in a single vehicle accident during the evening of January 16th northwest of North Buena Vista. Light freezing drizzle had coated the roads with a layer of ice. The man lost control of his pickup truck on a curve, slid off the road and hit a rock bluff head-on. He was pronounced dead at the scene by authorities.

A winter storm dropped around 5 inches of snow across Chickasaw County. A period of blizzard conditions occurred in the afternoon when winds gusted to around 35 mph and the combination of falling and blowing snow reduced the visibility to a quarter mile or less. Travel was not advised as roads were completely snow covered and some were closed by drifts. Schools across the county canceled classes for the day. The highest reported snowfall total was 5 inches in and around New Hampton and the highest recorded wind gust was 36 mph by a mesonet station north of Ionia.

Several schools across the county canceled classes for the day. The highest reported snowfall amount was 4.1 inches southwest of Elkader.

A period of blizzard conditions occurred in the afternoon when winds gusted to between 35 and 45 mph and the combination of falling and blowing snow reduced the visibility to a quarter mile or less. Travel was not advised as roads were completely snow covered and some were closed by drifts. Schools across the county canceled classes for the day. The highest reported snowfall total was 3 inches in Fayette and the highest recorded wind gust was 44 mph by the automated weather observing equipment at the Oelwein airport.

A Town of Genoa man was discovered dead in his residence by authorities on February 10th. The man's house did not have any heat and it is estimated that he passed away sometime on February 7th when temperatures were in the teens below zero and wind chills were 20 to 30 below zero. The official cause of death was listed as exposure/hypothermia.

An EF1 tornado developed between Rudd and Rockford and moved east before dissipating northwest of Charles City. The roof of a home near Rockford sustained some damage. Near the end of the path, a hog confinement building was heavily damaged, trees were downed and windows blown out of a house. Otherwise, the damage was limited to crops.

An EF0 tornado developed southwest of Oelwein and moved northeast into the city before dissipating. The tornado damaged the ticket booth, fencing and ripped metal siding off of stands at the high school football field. The tornado also blew out the sides of a greenhouse, tipped over the FFA's chicken coop and lifted but did not remove the roof on the main portion of the high school. At a restaurant, an air handler unit was ripped off and windows broken. Some crop and tree damage was noted southwest of the city as well.

A major flash flood hit Grant County during the afternoon of June 12th impacting the communities of Lancaster, Potosi, Tennyson, Ellenboro, and other rural areas.  Numerous rescues were performed from people trapped in cars, especially in the Potosi area where terrain enhanced the runoff from repeat thunderstorms.  Several homes on Hippie Hollow Road in Potosi Township were destroyed along with damage to as many as 600 homes elsewhere in the region.  Many highways and county roads suffered flood damage including major bridge and road infrastructure.

Runoff from heavy rains caused several roads to be damaged by water and mud slides.

Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Turkey River out of its banks in Elkader. The river crested almost eleven feet above the flood stage at 22.82 feet on the 30th. This was the fourth highest crest on record.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Turkey River out of its banks in Garber. The river crested over six feet above the flood stage at 23.39 feet. This was the fourth highest crest on record.
Runoff from heavy rains pushed the Yellow River out of its banks in Necedah. The river crested almost a foot over the flood stage at 15.97 feet on the 12th.

This very brief track was found in Sentinel satellite imagery and stayed in fields for its existence. Based on the location in the supercell, inflow wind trajectories along the left side of the track, and striation patterns in the fields, there is a high likelihood that this was an anti-cyclonic tornado.

Dense fog formed over Olmsted County during the morning of December 15th and reduced the visibility to less than a half mile. A six vehicle chain reaction accident occurred in the fog on U.S. Highway 52 north of Oronoco. One person was killed and four others sustained injuries.
A semi-truck and trailer were blown over at a truck stop in Floyd.
A roof was blown off a building near the entrance to Rudd Park.
Several buildings were flattened on a large farm just outside of Mitchell.
Quarter sized hail fell in Charles City.

This tornado formed in Butler County before crossing into southern Floyd County south of Marble Rock. The tornado remained on the ground for about 3 minutes in Floyd County as it moved across rural areas before dissipating south of Marble Rock. An NWS survey team determined this tornado to have an EF1 rating with damage limited to trees.

This tornado formed just north of Marble Rock and moved rapidly to the northeast before dissipating west of Charles City. An NWS survey team determined this tornado to have an EF1 rating. The tornado caused damage to homes, farm buildings and metal grain bins along with taking down power poles, power lines and trees.

The third tornado of the night in Floyd County formed just to the southwest of Rudd, moved northeast directly through the town and dissipated along Business U.S. Highway 18 on the north edge of town. Extensive damage occurred in the town with numerous homes sustaining damage with some roofs completely blown off. The roof of the library was removed with damage sustained to almost all the books in the building. A church on the north side of town also sustained heavy damage as did the towns water treatment plant. Water and power were not expected to be restored for several days. Classes for the Rudd-Rockford-Marble Rock school district were canceled for December 16th but the building in Rockford was open to the public for showers, warmth and served breakfast and lunch to those in need.
An EF1 tornado formed west of North Washington and moved to northeast for about 4 miles before dissipating. The tornado damaged trees and some farm outbuilding along its path.

The second tornado of the night in Chickasaw County formed southwest of Alta Vista and moved northeast before crossing into Howard County along County Line Road just east of the Little Wapsipinicon River. This tornado was rated EF0. The tornado damaged a greenhouse facility, otherwise, damage was limited to trees.

This tornado formed in Chickasaw County and moved into Howard County south of Elma along County Line Road just east of the Little Wapsipinicon River. The tornado moved rapidly northeast before dissipating south of Elma. Damage from this EF0 tornado was limited to trees and one farm.

This was the second tornado of the night in Howard County. This EF0 tornado formed northeast of Elma and moved northeast before dissipating east of Saratoga. Damage along the path was limited to trees and weak farm outbuildings.

This was the third tornado of the night in Howard County. This EF0 tornado formed west of Schley and move northeast before dissipating east of Davis Corners. This tornado removed the roof from a hog farm building, drove lumber through the side of a metal building and also damaged other outbuildings and trees. One house had broken windows and some damage from tree branches downed on it.

This was the fourth tornado of the night across Howard County. This EF0 tornado formed northeast of Schley and moved northeast before dissipating west of Cresco. This tornado caused damage to one farm where a house was effectively destroyed by large trees blown down on it. At another farm, the home sustained roof damage from a large tree downed on it along with broken windows and two metal outbuildings were destroyed with a third damaged.

This tornado originally developed in Worth County, Iowa, moved into Freeborn County, Minnesota before crossing into Mower County west of Lyle. The tornado was only on the ground for about one minute in Mower County as it moved northeast and dissipated. One farm was damaged by the tornado, otherwise, damage was limited to trees.

This was the second tornado of the night across Mower County. This EF1 tornado formed south of Racine, moved northeast just missing the town and then dissipated northeast of Racine. This tornado lifted the roof off a home and destroyed some farm buildings.
This EF0 tornado moved across rural portions of northwest Fillmore County west of Chatfield. The tornado produced damage to several farm buildings and trees along its path.

This was the second tornado of the night in Fillmore County. This narrow EF0 tornado moved across the eastern and northern parts of Preston. Houses, sheds, cars and trees were damaged along the path. The roofs of the fire department and city hall were both damaged.

This was the third tornado of the night in Fillmore County. This EF1 tornado developed northeast of Preston and moved northeast for about 2 miles before dissipating. Farm outbuildings and trees were damaged along the path.

This was the fourth tornado of the night in Fillmore County. This EF1 tornado formed just south of the tiny town of Arendahl and was only on the ground for one minute as it moved rapidly northeast. The damage was limited to a large grove of trees northeast of Arendahl.

This was the fifth tornado of the night in Fillmore County. This EF1 tornado formed south of Rushford and moved to the northeast before dissipating. The tornado destroyed some farm outbuildings and damaged trees along its path.
An EF1 tornado formed in far northern Dodge County north of West Concord and then moved northeast into Goodhue County. Two farms along the path of the tornado sustained minor damage.
An EF1 tornado developed southeast of Plainview and moved northeast across rural portions of southern Wabasha County. Farm outbuildings and trees were damaged along the path of the tornado.

An EF1 tornado formed west of Houston and moved northeast, passing to the east of Money Creek before dissipating just before the Winona County line. Several farms along the Root River sustained damage from this tornado.

An EF1 tornado formed on a ridge top southwest of Homer, moved northeast across Homer before moving out over the Mississippi River and into Trempealeau County, Wisconsin. The main damage occurred on the ridge top to trees and outbuildings. By the time the tornado reached Homer, it was weakening and damage was mainly limited to trees.
This short-lived EF0 tornado moved over rural areas southeast of Lewiston. Farm outbuildings, a garage and trees were damaged by the tornado.

This short-lived EF0 tornado likely formed over the Mississippi River, moved inland and across a portion of Perrot State Park before dissipating on the very western edge of Trempealeau. Extensive tree damage occurred in the state park and several homes were damaged when trees fell on them.

This EF1 tornado developed southeast of Osseo and moved northeast, crossing into Jackson County near County Highway G. The tornado passed through a farm where damage occurred to the house and outbuildings. Otherwise, mainly tree damage occurred.

This EF1 tornado developed in northeast Trempealeau County before moving into Jackson County near County Highway G southwest of Levis. The tornado continued to move northeast and dissipated along County Highway FF before reaching Interstate 94. Damage was primarily to trees with a couple of farm outbuildings also damaged.
This EF2 tornado developed in the far northern part of Jackson County north of Merillan and quickly moved northeast into Clark County. Damage was limited to trees.

This EF2 tornado developed in Jackson County and moved into the southwest part of Clark County east of Humbird. The tornado continued to move northeast before dissipating along County Highway B west of Sidney. This part of Clark County is heavily forested and thousands of trees were damaged.

This EF2 tornado developed southwest of Sidney and moved northeast across a heavily wooded area of southwest Clark County. Thousands of trees were damaged and one home was destroyed near Five Mile Creek.

This EF2 tornado developed northeast of Neillsville and moved northeast before dissipating after crossing State Highway 73 just north of Schofield Road. A farm took a direct hit from the tornado where a barn was shifted off its foundation, a truck moved almost 100 feet and roof damage to the house occurred.

This EF1 tornado formed west of Greenwood near the intersection of County Highways G and O. The tornado was only on the ground for about a mile but caused extensive damage to two farms. A barn roof was removed, a pole shed destroyed, power pole snapped and roof damage to an outbuilding.

This EF2 tornado developed in Chippewa County and crossed into Clark County after moving through Stanley. After moving into Clark County, the tornado moved across rural areas damaging farm outbuildings and trees.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Dodge County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. The highest recorded wind gust was 67 mph east of Kasson at a mesonet station.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Fillmore County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. The automated weather observing equipment at the Preston airport measured a wind gust of 60 mph. A county wide state of emergency was declared.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Houston County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Mower County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. The automated weather observing equipment at the Austin airport and a mesonet station near Dexter both measured a 58 mph wind gust.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Olmsted County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. The automated weather observing equipment at the Rochester airport measured a 77 mph gust. This was the second highest gust on record for this site. A garage was heavily damaged by a fire when the winds caused the flames from a burning transformer to spread to the garage. Power outages in and around Stewartville lasted into December 18th. The lack of power and heat on December 17th prompted classes to be canceled in the Stewartville school district and at one Rochester elementary school.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Winona County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. The automated weather observing equipment at the Winona airport measured a 52 mph gust.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Allamakee County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. Around 1300 customers lost power in Waukon for about an hour.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Chickasaw County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. A mesonet station near Ionia measured a 63 mph gust.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Howard County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Mitchell County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. A warming shelter was opened in Stacyville after the entire town lost power.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Winneshiek County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. A mesonet station near Frankville measured a 58 mph gust.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Adams County during the early morning of December 16th.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Buffalo County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. State Highway 88 was closed south of Cream because of downed power lines.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Clark County during the early morning of December 16th.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Crawford County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Grant County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. The automated weather observing equipment at the Platteville airport measured a 60 mph gust.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Jackson County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Juneau County during the early morning of December 16th. The automated weather observing equipment at the New Lisbon/Mauston airport measured a 58 mph gust.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across La Crosse County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. The automated weather observing equipment at the La Crosse airport measured a 68 mph gust. Several trees and power lines were blown down across the city of La Crosse causing some streets to be blocked off. Several vehicles were damaged by a downed tree on State Street.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Monroe County during the early morning of December 16th.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Richland County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Taylor County during the early morning of December 16th. The automated weather observing equipment at the Medford airport measured a 53 mph gust. A truck was damaged in Gilman when a 10 inch pine tree fell on it.
Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Trempealeau County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th.

Wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph were common across Vernon County during the late evening of December 15th into the early morning of the 16th. The automated weather observing equipment at the Viroqua airport measured a 62 mph gust.
A semi loaded with 30,000 pounds of perishable goods was blown over on Interstate 94. The driver sustained minor injuries.
One person was killed east of Rochester when a 40 foot pine tree was snapped off, fell and landed on the individual and his pickup truck.
The roofs to a workshop and a house were blown off and trees were uprooted in Whittlesey.
Trees and large branches were blown down in Ontario.
A metal pole shed was blown off its foundation just west of Cresco.
A metal machine building was destroyed west of Cresco.
An open air, metal outbuilding was destroyed north of Granger.
The tarp roof was blown off a livestock shed northeast of Lime Springs.

Icy conditions developed on Interstate 94 after a band of freezing drizzle moved across the area. A 38 vehicle accident occurred near Northfield and some vehicles were destroyed in a fire. No deaths occurred with about 20 minor injuries reported.
A 63 mph wind gust was measured with a private weather station north of Mabel.

The driver of a car was killed in a two vehicle accident on Interstate 90 near West Salem. Roads were snow covered and slippery from snow that fell from late morning through the afternoon. A semi was slowing down for backup traffic and a car behind the semi was unable to stop in the slippery conditions, slid under the trailer and became trapped. The driver of the car was killed as a result of the sustained injuries.
Trees and power poles were snapped off in Winona.
A small shed and a metal outbuilding were blown over and destroyed south of Charles City.
Part of a roof was blown off a house and a garage door blown in at a residence in Osage.
Two temporary structures for the Rotary Lights display in La Crosse were destroyed.
A barn was destroyed southwest of Eyota.
A hog barn and another barn were destroyed on a farm northwest of Osage.
A large tree was blown on to a business in Greenwood. Branches from the tree went through parts of the roof and the owner was temporarily trapped inside the business when the exit was blocked.
